warnings.warning: Table 4 states multiple-species capacity 200, while page 13 prose and the printed implementation set K=300.
Figure 9 is visibly a water-potential versus hyphal-extension plot but is captioned 'Relative Density of Woody Fibers by Time.'
Table 2 describes l_i as hyphal length but assigns mm/day; Equation 1 then differentiates l_i, so state and rate units do not close.
Equation 2 names pair coefficients c_ij, but the displayed matrix, formula, and code use one repeated off-diagonal c_i per row.
The appendix passes crowding-adjusted m into f and then multiplies the V update by the same unused-capacity factor again.
The factor returned to f is moisture factor a; temperature affects m but no separate temperature factor is passed to f.
Exact float equality for temperature and mapped water potential can fail when climate values do not match CSV grid values.
The printed implementation depends on missing Get_hyphal_rate and dataprocess modules and two missing CSV files.
The appendix omits executable multi-environment, diversity, sensitivity, and data-preprocessing workflows.
The five-three-two experiment keeps the first species, confounding richness with species identity and composition.
The paper infers convergence and robustness from a bounded heatmap without a convergence or global sensitivity analysis.
Table 1 reports R-squared values 0.4477, 0.3464, and 0.1568 despite small p-values, so significance should not be read as strong predictive fit.
Page 14 cites Appendix 7, but no numbered Appendix 7 exists in the paper.
The five selected city histories are scenario representatives and do not validate global fungal habitats.
